interpreterPremises.statement: Under the reviewed sandbox interpreter, stdlib json.loads(str) on each deep-nesting control (100000 nested arrays, about 200 KB; 100000 nested objects, about 600 KB, both under an unread top-level member) raises exactly RecursionError and does not crash
interpreterPremises.basis: CPython json scanner recursion guard (C-level limit in 3.12/3.13, stack-based check in 3.14, Python recursion limit for the pure-Python scanner). Not inspected; a premise only
interpreterPremises.probe: T00 and T16.1 call stdlib json.loads with no hooks on the control. The checker reportedly adds object_pairs_hook/parse_constant, which do not change array/object recursion depth (premise)
interpreterPremises.ifUnmet: T00 fails with 'M-HASH-D7-PREMISE P1 not met ... BLOCKED'. The RED is invalid: STOP. Do not tune DEEP and do not change the expectation. A segfault or kill is a STOP, not a result
interpreterPremises.portableAlternative: BLOCKED: an interpreter-independent refusal would need a tool depth limit that no approved clause defines

interpreterPremises.statement: Under the reviewed sandbox interpreter, stdlib json.loads(str) on the int-digit control (a 50000-digit decimal integer as the unread datum-schema 'index' value) raises exactly ValueError (not JSONDecodeError)
interpreterPremises.basis: CPython >= 3.11 default int_max_str_digits = 4300 (also in some 3.7-3.10 security releases). -I ignores PYTHONINTMAXSTRDIGITS and the argv has no -X int_max_str_digits. Not inspected; a premise only
interpreterPremises.ifUnmet: T00 fails with 'M-HASH-D7-PREMISE P2 not met ... BLOCKED'. The RED is invalid: STOP. Cost if the limit is absent: one 50000-digit conversion, milliseconds
interpreterPremises.portableAlternative: BLOCKED: an interpreter-independent refusal would need a tool integer-size limit that no approved clause defines

exceptionAssertions: Every negative asserts type(exc) is exactly ScriptHashInputError or exactly ScriptHashMismatchError, never just 'some ValueError'. Every implementation method first asserts that both classes are ValueError subclasses and that neither subclasses the other. Tripwire hooks raise TripwireError(Exception), which is not a ValueError; a consulted hook therefore surfaces as an error, and a hook that is consulted and then swallowed surfaces through the non-empty log assertion

d8Reliance: Nine controls (extra-finite-number, extra-overflow-1e999, extra-shallow-nesting, nan-top, infinity-top, neg-infinity-top, nan-preamble, deep-array-nesting, deep-object-nesting) add one extra member named 'x-d7-unread' (top level, or preamble for nan-preamble). Its positive controls (0.5, 1e999, shallow nesting) assume that an extra unread member is accepted, as already sanctioned for 1e999 in unread extra fields. This asserts no closure. If a future reviewed decision closes the schema, these positive controls fail visibly and need re-review; they never mask a closure. The int-digit and datum-index NaN/-Infinity controls use the existing CIP datum-schema 'index' slot, so they do not depend on D8
